chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi'e, who said:

I saw Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) performing rukūʿ with a bow lower than the bowing of every one I ever saw performing rukūʿ, and it was so that whenever he performed rukūʿ, he formed wings with his hands (spreading them).
ai.seo_question: What was the distinctive characteristic of Imam Al-Hasan's (AS) bowing posture during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the physical perfection (kamāl) of Imam al-Riḍā’s (or Imam al-Jawād’s, depending on the specific chain context in al-Kafi) prayer, emphasizing a deeper bow and the spreading of arms to facilitate the flow of blood to the head, a practice rooted in Prophetic tradition. It serves as a practical model for worshippers to emulate the Imam’s humility and physical grace during rukūʿ, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on following the Ahl al-Bayt’s ritual precision.
